title: AgiBotWorld-Beta v7 Qwen-signed canonical-E verification
summary: Five left-arm and five right-arm stride-5 high-motion windows across seven tasks. RGB checks approach/jaw lines and camera-spatial endpoint motion; signed polarity is frozen by the Qwen-aligned handedness contract plus the verified G1_120s mount, not inferred from a symmetric gripper image.
criteria: Both source flange frames use R_source_E=Ry(-90deg); left differs from obsolete v6 by Rx(pi), while right is unchanged.
Solid state80 E+X follows the flange-to-fingertip approach and E+Z lies on the physical jaw line; E+Y completes a right-handed frame.
Every displayed stride-5 span validates all five hidden packed one-step motion80 rows; stride changes visualization only.
The separate three-view audit reads explicit canonical T_world_E columns and compares packed state80/motion80 without dataset-specific renderer corrections.

datasets.conclusion: 10/10 selected windows are visually clear; 30/30 spans and 150/150 hidden one-step checks pass.

samples.reason: Left shorts-fold phase: approach and jaw axes are unobstructed; corrected Y/Z signs are visible.
Left towel handover: large centered gripper and separated triad with clear endpoint motion.
Left dishcloth phase: approach follows the tool and jaw/normal axes remain separated.
Left bottle-cap phase: gripper contact, approach, jaw line, and motion are all readable.
Left rope phase: full tool and triad remain visible over three endpoint spans.
Right shorts-fold phase: unchanged right correction remains aligned and motion is clear.
Right supermarket pick: large motion, visible contact, and separated axes.
Right towel lift: replacement high-motion window passes the 4-pixel visibility gate.
Right cutlery phase: large unobstructed triad and camera-frame endpoint displacement.
Right rope phase: approach/jaw lines and three endpoint transitions are visible.
